Awards were presented in a variety of categories, including Azure, Business Applications, Modern Work, Security, and Social Impact, as well as new categories for 2024 such as AI Innovation and Copilot. The global winners included Quisitive for Analytics, PwC for Building with AI, and Capgemini for Migration to Azure. The formal celebration of the winners is scheduled to take place at the MCAPS Start for Partners digital event in July and at Microsoft Ignite in November. <2> Microsoft announced it is delaying the broad release of its controversial "Recall" AI feature for new Copilot+ PCs, which was originally scheduled to launch on June 18, 2024. [3, 4] The feature, which works by periodically taking screenshots of a user's screen to create a searchable visual timeline, faced significant backlash from cybersecurity experts and privacy advocates who warned it could become a goldmine for hackers. [2, 3] Responding to the criticism, Microsoft stated the feature will now become an opt-in experience, require biometric authentication via Windows Hello for access, and receive additional data protection. [4] Instead of a wide release, Recall will first be made available in the coming weeks to the Windows Insider Program (WIP) to gather more feedback and ensure it meets high security standards before being rolled out to all Copilot+ PC users at a later, unspecified date. [8, 9, 10] <3> Microsoft announced on June 9, 2024, that three new Xbox Series X/S console options would be released for the 2024 holiday season. [8] The new models are a 1TB Xbox Series S in Robot White, an all-digital 1TB Xbox Series X in Robot White, and a 2TB Xbox Series X Special Edition in Galaxy Black. [8] <4> Following significant criticism from security and privacy advocates, Microsoft announced on June 7, 2024, that its controversial "Recall" feature would be an opt-in experience for users, rather than enabled by default. In a blog post, the company detailed several security enhancements to address the concerns. These measures include requiring Windows Hello enrollment and proof of presence to enable the feature and to later view the timeline or search its contents. Furthermore, Microsoft implemented "just in time" (JIT) decryption protected by Windows Hello Enhanced Sign-in Security (ESS), ensuring that the snapshots are only decrypted and accessible after the user authenticates. The search index database was also encrypted to provide an additional layer of security. <5> U.S. antitrust regulators have formalized an agreement to examine the roles of Microsoft, OpenAI, and Nvidia within the artificial intelligence sector to determine if they have violated antitrust laws. Under this arrangement, the Department of Justice (DOJ) will lead the investigation into the leading AI chipmaker, Nvidia. Concurrently, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) will scrutinize the conduct of OpenAI and its primary partner, Microsoft. This division of responsibility was negotiated between the two agencies and signals increasing regulatory focus on the rapidly growing AI industry. The FTC is also reportedly investigating whether Microsoft structured a recent $650 million deal with the AI startup Inflection in a way to avoid antitrust review. <6> On June 3, 2024, Microsoft announced a restructuring that includes the layoff of approximately 1,000 employees. The job cuts impact several divisions, including the Azure cloud unit and the mixed-reality organization responsible for the HoloLens 2 headset. Specifically, teams such as Azure for Operators and Mission Engineering, part of the Strategic Missions and Technologies (SMT) organization, were affected. The SMT division is known for its work on advanced technologies like quantum computing and space projects. While making these cuts, Microsoft affirmed its commitment to the Department of Defense's IVAS program and the continued sale and support of HoloLens 2. A company spokesperson described the layoffs as a regular part of managing the business and stated that Microsoft will continue to invest in strategic growth areas. This decision is part of a broader trend of workforce reductions in the tech industry as companies shift focus and resources, often towards artificial intelligence. <7> Microsoft announced the public preview of SQL Server 2025 during its Microsoft Build 2024 conference, which took place from May 21-23, 2024. [1, 2, 9] This new version brings significant enhancements, with a major focus on AI integration, performance, and developer tools. [5, 6] Key AI-related features include the introduction of new T-SQL syntax for AI queries, a native vector data type, and the integration of Microsoft's DiskANN library to improve vector search performance. [5] Performance and reliability have been improved through features like faster failover for availability groups, optimized locking, and the ability for administrators to limit tempdb consumption using the resource governor. [5] For developers, SQL Server 2025 adds a native JSON data type, support for regular expressions (regex) and fuzzy string matching, an optimized version of the sp_executesql stored procedure, and a new sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint procedure to interact with external REST APIs. [5] Concurrently, Microsoft also announced the general availability of SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) 21 and the public preview of Copilot in SSMS. [6] <8> Microsoft held its annual Build developer conference in Seattle, Washington, and online from May 21-23, 2024, attracting 4,000 in-person attendees and 200,000 registered virtual participants. The event's central theme was artificial intelligence, with Microsoft's CEO Satya Nadella discussing how AI is shaping the future of computing. Key announcements included the introduction of Copilot+ PCs, a new category of Windows computers with powerful neural processing units (NPUs) designed for AI tasks, and the new AI-powered "Recall" feature. The AI assistant, Copilot, was a major focus, with the unveiling of Team Copilot for integration into Microsoft 365 apps and the addition of OpenAI's GPT-4o model to the Copilot stack. For developers, Microsoft launched new capabilities in Copilot Studio for building custom AI assistants and enhanced Azure AI with updates to Azure AI Studio and Azure AI Search. The company also released new Azure virtual machines and introduced Real-Time Intelligence in Microsoft Fabric for managing time-sensitive data. Additionally, the conference covered cybersecurity, with new Responsible AI tools like Prompt Shields, and real-time video translation in the Microsoft Edge browser. <9> Microsoft's Vice Chair and President, Brad Smith, testified before the U.S. House of Representatives' Homeland Security Committee on June 13, 2024. The hearing, titled "A Cascade of Security Failures," was convened to scrutinize Microsoft's security culture following a damning Cyber Safety Review Board (CSRB) report on a 2023 cyber intrusion of Microsoft Exchange Online by a China-affiliated group known as Storm-0558. During his testimony, Smith unequivocally accepted responsibility for every issue cited in the CSRB report, which described the successful breach as a result of "a cascade of failures" by Microsoft. The committee also discussed other significant breaches, including the SolarWinds hack and a January 2024 intrusion by the Russian-affiliated group "Midnight Blizzard." Smith detailed Microsoft's 'Secure Future Initiative' (SFI), a company-wide effort launched in November 2023, to overhaul its security practices, enhance protections, and foster a security-first mindset to prevent future incidents. <10> On May 20, 2024, Microsoft held a special event to introduce a new category of personal computers branded as "Copilot+ PCs". [1] During the event, the company unveiled new Surface Pro and Surface Laptop models as the first devices in this lineup. [2, 3] These PCs are distinguished by their deep integration of AI at the core of the Windows 11 operating system and are powered exclusively by Qualcomm's Snapdragon X Elite and Snapdragon X Plus processors, which feature a high-performance Neural Processing Unit (NPU) capable of over 40 trillion operations per second. [1, 3, 5] Microsoft emphasized that this represents a complete reimagining of the PC, from the silicon to the operating system, designed to enhance productivity and creativity through advanced AI features. [1] In addition to the Surface devices, Microsoft announced that major manufacturing partners, including Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, and Samsung, would also be releasing Copilot+ PCs, with pre-orders available immediately and retail availability starting June 18, 2024. [3]
